notes: If reads are relative, stack ../ until you hit root. access.log / auth.log / proc-environ are the log-poisoning-to-RCE targets (inject PHP via User-Agent or SSH login, then include the log). php://filter base64-encodes source so PHP is not executed - decode the output to read config secrets.

recommended.note: Writes PHP into a server log via a controllable field (here the User-Agent), then includes that log through the LFI so the payload executes.
Reads the PHP source of a file instead of executing it, using the php://filter wrapper with a base64 encoder.

name: LFI - Interesting Files to Read

variations.label: Linux - logs (poisoning)
variations.description: Reads web server access or error logs for information gathering. Logs reveal visited URLs, client IPs, user agents, and error messages that may expose internal paths or misconfigurations.

variations.label: Windows
variations.description: Reads the hosts file for custom hostname-to-IP mappings. Reveals internal hostnames, development servers, and network topology that DNS queries might not show.

variations.label: PHP filter (source)
variations.description: PHP wrapper payload for LFI exploitation. Uses PHP stream wrappers to read source code (php://filter), inject code (php://input), or execute data URIs.
